questions.stem: This blood smear shows a white cell with a nucleus of more than five lobes. What does this finding most strongly indicate?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Megaloblastic anemia from impaired DNA synthesis (vitamin B12 or folate deficiency)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acute bacterial infection with a left shift

explanation.summary: A hypersegmented neutrophil (more than five nuclear lobes) reflects defective DNA synthesis and is characteristic of megaloblastic anemia caused by vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Bacterial infection instead causes a left shift with band forms, and the other options do not produce hypersegmentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: A hypersegmented neutrophil (more than five nuclear lobes) reflects defective DNA synthesis and is characteristic of megaloblastic anemia caused by vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Bacterial infection instead causes a left shift with band forms, and the other options do not produce hypersegmentation.

questions.stem: The red arrows in this peripheral blood smear point to small anucleate structures scattered among the red blood cells. What are they?

explanation.summary: The small purple bodies indicated are platelets (thrombocytes), anucleate cytoplasmic fragments derived from megakaryocytes. They are only 1 to 3 micrometers wide, far smaller than the surrounding biconcave red blood cells, and participate in clot formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The small purple bodies indicated are platelets (thrombocytes), anucleate cytoplasmic fragments derived from megakaryocytes. They are only 1 to 3 micrometers wide, far smaller than the surrounding biconcave red blood cells, and participate in clot formation.

questions.stem: This peripheral blood smear from an anemic patient shows the arrowed fragmented red cells. Their presence indicates which process?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia from mechanical RBC fragmentation

explanation.summary: The small, irregular fragments lacking central pallor are schistocytes. They are produced when red cells are sheared by intravascular microthrombi and are the hallmark of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The small, irregular fragments lacking central pallor are schistocytes. They are produced when red cells are sheared by intravascular microthrombi and are the hallmark of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.

questions.stem: This circulating lymphocyte on a peripheral smear shows a markedly convoluted, brain-like nuclear contour among normal red cells. What is this diagnostic cell called?

explanation.summary: The deeply grooved, gyriform nucleus is termed cerebriform; such cerebriform (Sezary) cells are the malignant CD4+ T lymphocytes of mycosis fungoides/Sezary syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: The deeply grooved, gyriform nucleus is termed cerebriform; such cerebriform (Sezary) cells are the malignant CD4+ T lymphocytes of mycosis fungoides/Sezary syndrome.
